title: Object-Oriented Programming with Java
description: Master OOP concepts through real-world Java applications and modern development practices

topics.title: Maya's Onboarding Challenge: Understanding Objects and Classes

blocks.title: The Codebase Tour
blocks.text: "Welcome to FinTech Solutions, Alex!" Maya said. The payment code looked intimidating, so she started with one idea: a class is a blueprint that groups related data and behavior, while each object is an independent instance created from that blueprint. Alex would begin by repairing a small PaymentProcessor class before exploring the larger system.

blocks.back: Classes are blueprints or templates that define the structure and behavior of objects

blocks.title: Debug a class and create its first object
blocks.prompt: The starter has three defects. Repair the field declaration, construct PaymentProcessor correctly, and finish the method call. Run the checks when the file looks valid.

checks.label: Declares the PaymentProcessor class
checks.hint: Use a public class declaration named PaymentProcessor.

checks.label: Terminates the private processorId field
checks.hint: Java field declarations end with a semicolon.

checks.label: Keeps processPayment(double amount)
checks.hint: Keep a void processPayment method with one double parameter.

checks.label: Creates an object with new PaymentProcessor()
checks.hint: Java object construction needs the new keyword.

checks.label: Calls processPayment and terminates the statement
checks.hint: End the processor.processPayment(100.00) call with a semicolon.

blocks.title: Building Your First Class
blocks.text: Maya asked Alex to model a user without exposing its state. They chose private fields for name, email, and account balance, then added methods that operate on those fields. When a parameter and a field represent the same idea, this.field makes the target object explicit and keeps updates readable.

blocks.front: Key idea from "Building Your First Class"?
blocks.back: Instance variables store the data that each object will have

blocks.title: Make object state explicit
blocks.prompt: The fields and methods exist, but updateProfile assigns parameters ambiguously. Change the two assignments so they explicitly update this object's fields.

checks.label: Keeps User state private
checks.hint: Keep name, email, and accountBalance as private fields.

checks.label: Updates this.name
checks.hint: Assign the newName parameter to this.name.

checks.label: Updates this.email
checks.hint: Assign the newEmail parameter to this.email.

checks.label: Exposes balance through a method
checks.hint: Keep the checkBalance method instead of exposing the field.

blocks.title: The Constructor Mystery
blocks.text: Maya explained that constructors establish a valid initial state when an object is created. One constructor can accept every required value, while a smaller overload can delegate to it with a safe default. Constructor delegation avoids duplicating initialization logic and keeps both creation paths consistent.

blocks.back: Constructors are special methods that initialize objects when they're created

blocks.title: Add a safe overloaded constructor
blocks.prompt: Keep the full constructor, then add a second User(String name, String email) constructor that delegates to it with a zero starting balance.

checks.label: Provides two User constructors
checks.hint: Add another public User constructor below the existing one.

checks.label: Keeps the three-parameter constructor
checks.hint: Keep the constructor that accepts name, email, and initialBalance.

checks.label: Adds the name-and-email constructor
checks.hint: The overload should accept only name and email.

checks.label: Delegates with a zero balance
checks.hint: Call this(name, email, 0.0); as the overload's first statement.

blocks.title: Objects in Action
blocks.text: A transfer is useful only when objects collaborate correctly. The sender must approve and apply the debit before the receiver is credited. Maya asked Alex to trace both success and failure paths so the method never reports success while silently skipping the receiver update.

blocks.back: Objects can interact with each other through method calls

blocks.title: Finish the object interaction
blocks.prompt: The sender is charged, but the receiver never gets the money. Complete the successful branch so the two objects interact correctly.

checks.label: Defines transferMoney with two users and an amount
checks.hint: Keep the transferMoney method signature.

checks.label: Checks sender.makePayment(amount)
checks.hint: Charge the sender before crediting the receiver.

checks.label: Calls receiver.receivePayment(amount)
checks.hint: Inside the successful branch, call receiver.receivePayment(amount);

checks.label: Returns false when payment fails
checks.hint: Keep the failure return after the if block.

blocks.title: Code Review and Best Practices
blocks.text: During review, Maya focused on invariants rather than style alone. A User should never begin with a missing name or a negative balance. Validating constructor inputs before assignment makes failure immediate, keeps invalid objects out of the system, and gives callers a clear error to handle.

blocks.front: Key idea from "Code Review and Best Practices"?
blocks.back: Follow Java naming conventions: PascalCase for classes, camelCase for methods and variables

blocks.title: Protect the User constructor
blocks.prompt: Add fail-fast validation: reject a missing or blank name and reject a negative initial balance with IllegalArgumentException before assigning fields.

checks.label: Rejects a null or blank name
checks.hint: Check null plus either trim().isEmpty() or isBlank().

checks.label: Rejects a negative initial balance
checks.hint: Add a condition for initialBalance < 0.

checks.label: Throws IllegalArgumentException
checks.hint: Each invalid input should throw a clear IllegalArgumentException.

checks.label: Keeps explicit field assignments
checks.hint: Keep the field assignments after validation succeeds.
